text:
The Sharks took more shots, more shot attempts and more power plays than the Kings did. They also lost 7-2, which tells you most of what you need to know about where the night went wrong for San Jose, and how right it went for Adrian Kempe.

Kempe scored 1:23 in, off an Artemi Panarin feed, and added a slap shot at 16:09 of the first. Quinton Byfield made it 3-0 on the power play at 18:38, with Panarin and Kempe assisting. Los Angeles owned that period, out-chancing San Jose 2.08 to 1.05 in expected goals, the quality of each side's chances. Macklin Celebrini got one back on a power play early in the second, but Erik Haula and then Kempe, on the power play at 15:51 for the hat trick, pushed it to 5-1. Haula's goal also gave Kenny Connors, a 2022 fourth-round pick out of UMass, his first NHL point.

Joel Armia tipped in a sixth early in the third. Ivar Stenberg scored on a 2% power-play chance for San Jose, and Byfield tipped in his second, also on the power play, to finish it. Kempe ended with three goals and an assist; Panarin had four assists, every one of them on a Kempe or Byfield goal. When those two are connecting like that, there isn't much a goalie can do about it, though this goalie could have done more.

The scoreboard flatters the Kings, though. Replay every shot and Los Angeles wins 71% of the time, which is a comfortable win, not a five-goal one. San Jose outshot them 32 to 27 and took 67 shot attempts to 57. The difference was Yaroslav Askarov, who stopped 20 of 27 and allowed 3.1 goals more than his shots deserved. At the other end, Darcy Kuemper stopped 30 of 32.

Celebrini played 22:42 and had five shots, and the Sharks' power play did its job twice in six tries. They won the first meeting this season, 5-4 in overtime on Oct. 3. This one is the kind of night a young team should file under goaltending and special teams, not effort, and move on.
headline: Kempe and Panarin turn a close fight into a 7-2 rout
